PSYC 101.description: An introduction to and survey of the basic concepts and findings within the field of psychology.
PSYC 101.subject: PSYC
PSYC 101.title: Introduction to Psychology

PSYC 103.description: Introduction to theories and processes underlying and facilitating human adjustment in the community, family, and workplace.
PSYC 103.subject: PSYC
PSYC 103.title: Psychology of Adjustment

PSYC 120.description: Overview of disciplines and careers in psychology. Students will discover career-related interests and options at the bachelor’s and post-baccelaureate levels and will be introduced to academic advising, curricular and extracurricular opportunities and academic resources available to support them toward their career goals.
PSYC 120.subject: PSYC
PSYC 120.title: Professional Development in Psychology

PSYC 220.description: Introduction to statistical methods essential for psychological research.
PSYC 220.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 101; C or better in MATH 111 or equivalent or Math placement score.
PSYC 220.subject: PSYC
PSYC 220.title: Psychological Statistics

PSYC 221.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 220.
PSYC 221.subject: PSYC
PSYC 221.title: Research Methods in Psychology

PSYC 300.description: Psychological, physiological, and sociological factors of human sexual behavior and attitudes.
PSYC 300.subject: PSYC
PSYC 300.title: Human Sexual Behavior

PSYC 301.description: The psychological, physiological, and social characteristics of marriage.
PSYC 301.subject: PSYC
PSYC 301.title: Psychology of Marriage

PSYC 310.description: Women’s experiences: childhood and adolescence, work, family, cultural images, adjustment, and social change.
PSYC 310.subject: PSYC
PSYC 310.title: Psychology of Women

PSYC 320.description: The development of the religious consciousness and its various expressions, the psychological dynamics of growth and conversion, response to crisis, and the relation of spiritual practice to health and wholeness.
PSYC 320.subject: PSYC
PSYC 320.title: Psychology of Religion

PSYC 330.description: Psychological theory and research as it applies to African Americans. Explores Africentric and other perspectives and roles of culture, racism, and historical phenomena.
PSYC 330.subject: PSYC
PSYC 330.title: Psychology and the African-American Experience

PSYC 350.description: Psychological techniques applied to various industrial problem areas, such as management and supervision, morale, efficiency, training, personnel selection and placement, and relations among personnel.
PSYC 350.subject: PSYC
PSYC 350.title: Industrial Psychology

PSYC 360.description: Uses of psychological knowledge and techniques in practical contexts; clinical, school, industrial, consumer, and environmental psychology.
PSYC 360.subject: PSYC
PSYC 360.title: Applied Psychology

PSYC 370.description: Theories, controversies, and research findings on the nature of various states of consciousness; topics such as sleep/dreams, hypnosis, drug-induced states, and psychic phenomena.
PSYC 370.subject: PSYC
PSYC 370.title: Psychology of Consciousness

PSYC 380.description: The role of sports in socialization, personality development and competence, including: spectator-performer interactions, motivation, competition effects; and the application of psychological techniques to performance enhancement.
PSYC 380.subject: PSYC
PSYC 380.title: Sport Psychology

PSYC 399.description: Reading-based course, closely supervised project, or research experience for psychology minors and other non-psychology majors. Focus on a psychological issue of personal interest or to assist with ongoing research projects under the supervision of a psychology faculty member. 3-4 hours per week for each enrolled credit hour. A written product and/or oral presentation is required. Approved contract required. May be repeated for up to six credits. Not for psychology major credit.
PSYC 399.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 101.
PSYC 399.subject: PSYC
PSYC 399.title: Independent Study or Research Experience for Non-Psychology Majors

PSYC 400.description: Research and applications concerning the acquisition of new behavior and knowledge, including accounts based on classical and instrumental conditioning and on information-processing models.
PSYC 400.subject: PSYC
PSYC 400.title: Survey of Learning and Memory

PSYC 401.description: Introduction to psychosocial factors in physical activity. Topics include mental health effects of exercise, behavior change theories applied to physical activity, and physical activity determinants and interventions.
PSYC 401.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 101.
PSYC 401.subject: PSYC
PSYC 401.title: Psychology of Physical Activity

PSYC 405.description: Research and theories on sensory memory, attention, short-term and working memory, human learning and forgetting, imagery, long-term memory, speech perception, reading, language, thinking and problem solving, and decision making.
PSYC 405.subject: PSYC
PSYC 405.title: Cognitive Psychology

PSYC 410.description: Covers the classification, diagnosis, etiological theories, and treatments of the major mental and emotional disorders.
PSYC 410.subject: PSYC
PSYC 410.title: Behavioral and Mental Disorders

PSYC 420.description: Psychological development from conception to late adulthood. Topics include physical, cognitive, and social processes associated with development at each stage of the life cycle.
PSYC 420.subject: PSYC
PSYC 420.title: Survey of Developmental Psychology

PSYC 430.description: Introduction to theory and research in social psychology from a psychological viewpoint. Topics include social perception, social cognition, attitudes, interpersonal relationships, aggression, prosocial behavior, and group processes.
PSYC 430.subject: PSYC
PSYC 430.title: Survey of Social Psychology

PSYC 432.description: This course provides an overview of psychological, social, physical, and emotional issues related to men’s lives. Major topics include: gender construction, men and work, men and health, men in relationships, male sexualities, men in families, and masculinities in the media and popular culture.
PSYC 432.subject: PSYC
PSYC 432.title: Men and Masculinities

PSYC 440.description: Covers the major theories and research on personality and the dynamics of human motivation.
PSYC 440.subject: PSYC
PSYC 440.title: Survey of Personality

PSYC 450.description: Processing of information from the environment. Physiological, physical, psychological, and contextual determinants of perception.
PSYC 450.subject: PSYC
PSYC 450.title: Sensation and Perception

PSYC 455.description: Function of the brain including basic neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and neurochemistry, neural systems, and psychopharmacology as it relates to behavior.
PSYC 455.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 101.
PSYC 455.subject: PSYC
PSYC 455.title: Introduction to Neuroscience

PSYC 460.description: How the brain mediates simple and complex behavior and how we can apply basic research about the brain to real world problems.
PSYC 460.subject: PSYC
PSYC 460.title: Brain and Behavior

PSYC 465.description: Application of psychological theories and assessment and treatment methodologies for health maintenance and the diagnosis and treatment of illness.
PSYC 465.subject: PSYC
PSYC 465.title: Health Psychology

PSYC 470.description: Introduction to the linguistic component of human cognition. Properties of speech, the organization of language in the mind/brain, cross-linguistic universals, child language acquisition, and aspects of adult language processing.
PSYC 470.subject: PSYC
PSYC 470.title: Introduction to Language Sciences

PSYC 474.description: Bilingual language development, social and cultural aspects of bilingualism, the bilingual brain, bilingualism throughout the lifespan.
PSYC 474.subject: PSYC
PSYC 474.title: Cognitive and Social Aspects of Bilingualism

PSYC 475.description: The scientific basis of clinical psychology. Topics include history, theory, research, ethics, and best practices. For students interested in graduate school in psychology or other mental health professions.
PSYC 475.subject: PSYC
PSYC 475.title: Survey of Clinical Psychology

PSYC 476.description: Introduction to theory and research in sleep science from a psychological viewpoint. Topics include sleep, dreaming, consciousness, health, and sleep disorders.
PSYC 476.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in NSCI 300, PSYC 455, or PSYC 460.
PSYC 476.subject: PSYC
PSYC 476.title: Psychology of Sleep

PSYC 480.description: This course provides an introduction to theories and research in the study of psychosocial issues of racial, ethnic and cultural groups.
PSYC 480.subject: PSYC
PSYC 480.title: Multi-Cultural Psychology

PSYC 487.description: Application of knowledge from other areas of psychology to the study of the role of the individual in the community.
PSYC 487.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 101 and at least 3 hours in psychology at 400 level or above.
PSYC 487.subject: PSYC
PSYC 487.title: Community Psychology

PSYC 489.description: Supervised, structured field experience in a community agency, applying psychological principles, theory, and research. May be repeated once for credit.
PSYC 489.subject: PSYC
PSYC 489.title: Community Psychology Practicum

PSYC 490.description: An undergraduate service-learning class focused on teaching assistantships in the Psychology Department, which applies research methods, cognitive and educational psychology concepts to student experience.
PSYC 490.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B+ or better in PSYC 101.
PSYC 490.subject: PSYC
PSYC 490.title: Assistantship in Teaching of Psychology (AToP)

PSYC 495.description: A supervised experiential course in psychology. Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and Office of Academic Programs is required for undergraduate students.
PSYC 495.subject: PSYC
PSYC 495.title: Internship in Psychology

PSYC 498.description: Closely supervised project or research experience in psychology; assist with ongoing research projects. 3-4 hours per week for each enrolled credit hour. A written product and/or oral presentation is required. Approved contract required. May be repeated for up to six credits.
PSYC 498.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 9 hours of Psychology coursework (PSYC 101-PSYC 699).
PSYC 498.subject: PSYC
PSYC 498.title: Research Experience

PSYC 499.description: Reading-based course. Focus on a psychological issue of personal interest under the supervision of a psychology faculty member. 3-4 hours per week for each enrolled credit hour. A written product and/or oral presentation is required. Approved contract required. May be repeated for up to six credits.
PSYC 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 101 and 9 hours of additional Psychology coursework (PSYC 101-PSYC 699).
PSYC 499.subject: PSYC
PSYC 499.title: Independent Study

PSYC 501.description: Application of research in experimental psychology to ergonomics, the design of human-environment systems, with emphasis on work settings.
PSYC 501.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 101 and 9 hours of upper-level courses all in psychology, business, engineering, or nursing.
PSYC 501.subject: PSYC
PSYC 501.title: Human Factors Psychology

PSYC 503.description: Research and theoretical considerations of substance abuse. Pharmacological, sociological, psychological, medical, economic, forensic, and other relevant research and treatment disciplines.
PSYC 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 450 or PSYC 455 or PSYC 460.
PSYC 503.subject: PSYC
PSYC 503.title: Psychology of Drug Use and Effects

PSYC 506.description: Theories of speech perception, linguistic theories of syntax and semantics, the brain mechanisms underlying language, the development of language in children, and the role of language in thought.
PSYC 506.subject: PSYC
PSYC 506.title: Psychology of Language

PSYC 507.description: Research and theories on the role of the brain in facets of cognitive behavior, including attention, short-term and working memory, perception, language, executive function, thinking, and problem solving.
PSYC 507.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 405.
PSYC 507.subject: PSYC
PSYC 507.title: Cognitive Neuroscience

PSYC 510.description: Theories, description, and assessment of child behavior problems and disorders; methods of intervention.
PSYC 510.subject: PSYC
PSYC 510.title: Child Behavioral and Mental Disorders

PSYC 520.description: Examination of development from conception through older childhood. Specific cognitive and social processes will be given in-depth study.
PSYC 520.subject: PSYC
PSYC 520.title: Psychology of Child Development

PSYC 521.description: Theories and research examining social, emotional, and intellectual development in adolescence. Explores influence of family, peer, school, and cultural contexts.
PSYC 521.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 420 or graduate standing.
PSYC 521.subject: PSYC
PSYC 521.title: Psychology of Adolescence

PSYC 522.description: Developmental changes in abilities, personality, and behavior which occur between adolescence and old age.
PSYC 522.subject: PSYC
PSYC 522.title: Psychology of Early and Middle Adulthood

PSYC 523.description: Psychological, social, and biological phenomena associated with maturity and aging.
PSYC 523.subject: PSYC
PSYC 523.title: Psychology of Aging

PSYC 526.description: Etiology, prevention of, and intervention in behavioral, social, emotional, educational, and psychological problems in children and youth at risk.
PSYC 526.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 410 or PSYC 420 or equivalent.
PSYC 526.subject: PSYC
PSYC 526.title: Prevention of Psychological Problems in Children and Youth at Risk

PSYC 528.description: Characteristics, causes, needs, and intervention strategies for individuals with neurodevelopmental differences including a focus on biological, societal, cognitive, physical, and social/emotional strengths and challenges.
PSYC 528.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 420 or PSYC 520.
PSYC 528.subject: PSYC
PSYC 528.title: Psychology of Neurodevelopmental Disorders

PSYC 529.description: Children with average/above average intelligence and specific learning impairments; diagnostic and remedial techniques. Offered by both the College of Education and the Department of Psychology.
PSYC 529.subject: PSYC
PSYC 529.title: Nature of Students with Specific Learning Disabilities

PSYC 530.description: Intensive study of topics selected from the field of social psychology.
PSYC 530.subject: PSYC
PSYC 530.title: Advanced Social Psychology

PSYC 550.description: Intensive study of topics selected from the field of sensation and perception.
PSYC 550.subject: PSYC
PSYC 550.title: Advanced Sensation and Perception

PSYC 560.description: Intensive study of topics selected from the field of neuroscience. Course may be repeated for credit under different topics.
PSYC 560.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in NSCI 300, PSYC 455, or PSYC 460, for undergraduates.
PSYC 560.subject: PSYC
PSYC 560.title: Advanced Topics in Neuroscience

PSYC 570.description: Practice in the methods of scientific inquiry and the dissemination of research in neuroscience.
PSYC 570.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in NSCI 300, PSYC 455, or PSYC 460.
PSYC 570.subject: PSYC
PSYC 570.title: Neuroscience Laboratory

PSYC 571.description: Methods of observation and experimentation in cognitive neuroscience. Two lectures and one three-hour laboratory per week.
PSYC 571.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PSYC 221, PSYC 507 and one of PSYC 455/NSCI 300 or PSYC 460; or Graduate Student standing.
PSYC 571.subject: PSYC
PSYC 571.title: Cognitive Neuroscience Laboratory

PSYC 572.description: Practice in the experimental techniques used in the study of cognitive psychology. Two lectures and one three-hour laboratory per week.
PSYC 572.subject: PSYC
PSYC 572.title: Cognitive Psychology Laboratory

PSYC 574.description: Concepts and principles in the study of sensation and perception in the laboratory. Two lectures and one three-hour laboratory per week.
PSYC 574.subject: PSYC
PSYC 574.title: Sensation and Perception Laboratory

PSYC 575.description: Methods of observation and experimentation on human psychological development. Two lectures and one three-hour laboratory per week.
PSYC 575.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in PSYC 220 and PSYC 221.
PSYC 575.subject: PSYC
PSYC 575.title: Developmental Psychology Laboratory

PSYC 576.description: Practice in the methods of scientific inquiry and the dissemination of research in sleep science.
PSYC 576.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in PSYC 476; C or better in either NSCI 300, PSYC 455, or PSYC 460; or graduate standing.
PSYC 576.subject: PSYC
PSYC 576.title: Psychology of Sleep Laboratory

PSYC 580.description: Advanced analysis of the uses and applications of statistics to research in psychology, and interpretation of statistics in the psychological literature.
PSYC 580.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in PSYC 221 or graduate student standing.
PSYC 580.subject: PSYC
PSYC 580.title: Intermediate Statistics for Psychologists

PSYC 583.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of measuring psychological attributes. Emphasis on test construction in a laboratory setting. Hands-on experience in designing, administering, and analyzing psychological tests and measures.
PSYC 583.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in PSYC 220 and PSYC 221.
PSYC 583.subject: PSYC
PSYC 583.title: Psychological Tests and Measurement

PSYC 584.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 9 hours in psychology at 400 level or above.
PSYC 584.subject: PSYC
PSYC 584.title: History and Systems of Psychology

PSYC 589.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PSYC 589.subject: PSYC
PSYC 589.title: Selected Topics in Psychology

PSYC 598.description: Planning and execution of supervised research in psychology on a project with significant original contributions. Not intended as a research assistant position to assist professors or graduate students in their research. 3 hours per week for each enrolled credit hour. A written product and/or oral presentation is required. Approved contract required. May be repeated for up to six credits.
PSYC 598.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 15 hours Psychology coursework (PSYC 101-PSYC 699), or departmental approval.
PSYC 598.subject: PSYC
PSYC 598.title: Individual Research

PSYC 599.description: Planning and execution of supervised research in psychology on a project with significant original contributions. Not intended as a research assistant position to assist professors or graduate students in their research. May be a continuation of a project from PSYC 598 . 3 hours per week for each enrolled credit hour. A written product and/or oral presentation is required. Approved contract required.
PSYC 599.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 15 hours of Psychology coursework (PSYC 101-PSYC 699), or departmental approval.
PSYC 599.subject: PSYC
PSYC 599.title: Advanced Individual Research

PSYC 700.description: Introduction to gerontology from the fields of demography, psychology, sociology, social welfare, and economics.
PSYC 700.subject: PSYC
PSYC 700.title: Psychosocial Approaches to Gerontology

PSYC 701.description: A combination of lecture and practicum experiences emphasizing the application of behavioral assessment and intervention techniques in educational, institutional, and home settings. Students receive individual and group supervision throughout the semester.
PSYC 701.subject: PSYC
PSYC 701.title: Behavioral Assessment and Intervention with Children and Youth

PSYC 702A.description: Functional organization of the nervous system; research and theories of the neurological bases of behavior.
PSYC 702A.subject: PSYC
PSYC 702A.title: Basics of Neuroscience

PSYC 702B.description: Research and theories on attention, memory, language, thinking, and other cognitive processes.
PSYC 702B.subject: PSYC
PSYC 702B.title: Basics of Cognitive Psychology

PSYC 702C.description: Research and theories of psychological development across the lifespan.
PSYC 702C.subject: PSYC
PSYC 702C.title: Basics of Developmental Psychology

PSYC 702D.description: Research and theories of instrumental conditioning, classical conditioning, learning, and motivation.
PSYC 702D.subject: PSYC
PSYC 702D.title: Basics of Learning and Motivation

PSYC 702E.description: This course covers basic principles of sound experimental design, including such topics as internal and external validity, subject selection factors, and techniques for reducing sampling error and minimizing bias. In addition, the course will discuss practical limitations to ideal experimental design and have students identify the design conventions specific to their field of study.
PSYC 702E.subject: PSYC
PSYC 702E.title: Experimental Design

PSYC 703A.description: Research and theories of cognitive neuroscience.
PSYC 703A.subject: PSYC
PSYC 703A.title: Integration across Cognitive Psychology and Neuroscience

PSYC 703C.description: Research and theories of cognitive development.
PSYC 703C.subject: PSYC
PSYC 703C.title: Integration across Developmental and Cognitive Psychology

PSYC 703D.description: Presentation of research and theories that cross different areas within psychology.
PSYC 703D.subject: PSYC
PSYC 703D.title: Integration across Areas of Psychology

PSYC 704.description: Offered for an interdisciplinary student clientele interested in group processes and structures. Training is provided in observational methods and techniques of group assessment. Laboratory and field study required.
PSYC 704.subject: PSYC
PSYC 704.title: Group Dynamics

PSYC 705.description: Contemporary trends in systematic approaches and behavior theories.
PSYC 705.subject: PSYC
PSYC 705.title: Psychological Systems and Theories

PSYC 706.description: Research and theories of processes in judgment, choice, and decision making.
PSYC 706.subject: PSYC
PSYC 706.title: Seminar in Judgment and Decision Making

PSYC 709.description: Quantitative methods for graduate students in psychology and other behavioral sciences. Emphasizes logical/intuitive understanding of the basic techniques, focuses heavily on the application of these methods to psychological research. Three lecture/discussion hours and a one-hour scheduled lab per week.
PSYC 709.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: introductory course in statistics, psychology or mathematics.
PSYC 709.subject: PSYC
PSYC 709.title: Basic Quantitative Methods in the Analysis of Behavioral Data I

PSYC 710.description: A continuation of PSYC 709 . Three lecture/discussion hours and a one-hour scheduled lab per week.
PSYC 710.subject: PSYC
PSYC 710.title: Basic Quantitative Methods in the Analysis of Behavioral Data II

PSYC 713.description: Consideration of basic issues in evaluation of children, such as reliability, validity, item selection, standardization groups, criterion-referenced vs. norm-based testing, ethics, etc. Includes presentations via various instructional modes of a wide range of psychoeducational assessment procedures with a wide variety of children.
PSYC 713.subject: PSYC
PSYC 713.title: Survey of Psychoeducational Tests and Assessment

PSYC 714.description: A combination of lectures and practicum concerned with interviewing, behavioral observation and analysis, and cognitive-intellectual assessment. Requires involvement in school psychology training-service centers in the schools.
PSYC 714.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: acceptance in graduate psychology department program.
PSYC 714.subject: PSYC
PSYC 714.title: Cognitive Assessment

PSYC 715.description: A combination of lectures and practicum concerned with assessment of perceptual-motor processes, academic achievement, and personality and interpersonal skills. Requires involvement in school psychology training-service centers in the schools.
PSYC 715.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 714 and acceptance in graduate psychology department program.
PSYC 715.subject: PSYC
PSYC 715.title: Academic Assessment

PSYC 716.description: Consideration, via lecture and/or practicum, of special areas of psychoeducational assessment. Topics will include infant assessment, criterion-referenced assessment, and assessment of neurological problems.
PSYC 716.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PSYC 714, Acceptance in Department of Psychology graduate program.
PSYC 716.subject: PSYC
PSYC 716.title: Behavioral/Affective Assessment

PSYC 717.description: Issues, theories, and research on personality.
PSYC 717.subject: PSYC
PSYC 717.title: Survey of Personality Theories

PSYC 720.description: Integration of theory, research, and practice in child clinical and family psychology. Focus on systemic, behavioral, and other orientations in the treatment of children and families.
PSYC 720.subject: PSYC
PSYC 720.title: Psychological Interventions with Children and Families

PSYC 721.description: Theoretical, empirical, and methodological issues in the development of psychopathology or resilience in children, adolescents, and families. Emphasis on research topics related to nature, course, and etiology.
PSYC 721.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: acceptance in graduate psychology department or consent of instructor.
PSYC 721.subject: PSYC
PSYC 721.title: Developmental Psychopathology and Resilience

PSYC 725.description: Seminar emphasizing a critical analysis of psychotherapy systems and theories.
PSYC 725.subject: PSYC
PSYC 725.title: Systems and Theories of Psychological Intervention

PSYC 726.description: A survey of clinical disorders, their origins and characteristics. Includes a review of contemporary diagnostic systems, research, and theory.
PSYC 726.subject: PSYC
PSYC 726.title: Psychological Problems and Resilience

PSYC 727.description: Survey of theoretical foundations, research and practice in community psychology. Topics include prevention, social systems intervention, community participation, innovation in community service delivery systems, and community change processes.
PSYC 727.subject: PSYC
PSYC 727.title: Foundations of Community Psychology

PSYC 728.description: Designated to accompany Psychology 727. Laboratory will target specific problems, resources, or populations and will provide students with elementary exposure to a community system.
PSYC 728.subject: PSYC
PSYC 728.title: Laboratory in Community Study

PSYC 732.description: Overview of relationships between brain structures and function and the assessment of cognitive and emotional behavior in adults and children.
PSYC 732.subject: PSYC
PSYC 732.title: Clinical Neuropsychology

PSYC 733.description: Applications of neuropsychological theory and research to the study of the learning process, with emphasis upon assessment and intervention with learning disabilities.
PSYC 733.subject: PSYC
PSYC 733.title: Neuropsychological Syndromes in Childhood|

PSYC 734.description: Assessment procedures for screening neuropsychological factors in individuals with neurobehavioral deficits.
PSYC 734.subject: PSYC
PSYC 734.title: Neuropsychological Screening and Assessment

PSYC 735.description: The effect of drugs upon internal psycho-physiological functioning and upon the behavior of human and animal subjects. Particular emphasis will be given to the psychoactive drugs.
PSYC 735.subject: PSYC
PSYC 735.title: Survey of Psychopharmacology

PSYC 742.description: Focus on understanding the theoretical bases of consultation and developing the skills necessary for the practice of mental health consultation.
PSYC 742.subject: PSYC
PSYC 742.title: Consultation and Systems Interventions

PSYC 743.description: Continues the practicum begun in Psychology 742 and develops the skills of administrative mental health consultation and evaluation of consultation programs.
PSYC 743.subject: PSYC
PSYC 743.title: Theory and Practice of Mental Health Consultation II

PSYC 745.description: Analysis of the organization as a complex interaction system.
PSYC 745.subject: PSYC
PSYC 745.title: Organizational Behavior

PSYC 749.description: Fundamental, conceptual and empirical knowledge regarding dimensions of diversity, social inequality and the application of this knowledge to psychological research, teaching and practice. Restricted to psychology students. Non-Psychology students need instructor permission to register.
PSYC 749.subject: PSYC
PSYC 749.title: Principles of Human Diversity

PSYC 750.description: Women’s diversity explored through research on personality, stereotypes, status and power, biological aspects, socialization, sexuality, relationships, mothering, work and achievement, violence against women, psychological disorders, and feminist therapies.
PSYC 750.subject: PSYC
PSYC 750.title: Psychology of Women

PSYC 751.description: Historical and contemporary dimensions of social inequality centered in race, social class, gender, and sexuality.
PSYC 751.subject: PSYC
PSYC 751.title: Race, Class, Gender, and Sexuality

PSYC 760.description: The presentation of ethics in research and practice in clinical-community psychology and the discussion of current professional issues. Covering history and systems in psychology and providing in depth training on the ethical conduct of research.
PSYC 760.subject: PSYC
PSYC 760.title: Issues and Ethics in Health Services Psychology

PSYC 761.description: Develop assessment skills through interviewing, observation, performance testing, and report writing. Experience includes assessment of individuals, couples, and/or families from a variety of perspectives. Didactic/practicum.
PSYC 761.subject: PSYC
PSYC 761.title: Psychological Assessment I

PSYC 762.description: Theory of measurement and the construction of measures specific to clinical and community psychology. Intellectual achievement, objective personality, and projective measures. Didactic/practicum.
PSYC 762.subject: PSYC
PSYC 762.title: Psychological Assessment II

PSYC 763.description: Conceptualization of cases involving psychological measures. Clients include individuals, couples, and families. Didactic/practicum. May be repeated for up to 4 credits.
PSYC 763.subject: PSYC
PSYC 763.title: Clinical Psychology Assessment III

PSYC 765.description: A closely supervised 20-hour-per-week externship in the techniques of psychological services in school systems. Staff.
PSYC 765.subject: PSYC
PSYC 765.title: Externship in School Psychology

PSYC 770.description: Issues, research, and theories in social psychology.
PSYC 770.subject: PSYC
PSYC 770.title: Survey of Social Psychology

PSYC 772.description: Nonquantitative aspects of research methodology and experimental design in laboratory and field settings. A critical investigation of artifacts and ethical issues in behavioral research.
PSYC 772.subject: PSYC
PSYC 772.title: Research Approaches to Human Behavior

PSYC 773.description: Supervised training in the conduct of empirical research in clinical-community psychology. May be repeated once for credit.
PSYC 773.subject: PSYC
PSYC 773.title: Research in Clinical-Community Psychology

PSYC 777.description: The study of human behavior and satisfaction in relation to the natural and person-made environment. Topics include environmental stress, risk, social ecology of families, behavior setting theory, and person-environmental relationships.
PSYC 777.subject: PSYC
PSYC 777.title: Environmental Psychology
